result.abstractText: Lignin-based carbon fibers (LCFs) with graphitized structures decorated on their surfaces were successfully prepared using the simultaneous catalyst loading and chemical stabilization of melt-spun lignin fibers, followed by quick carbonization functionalized as catalytic graphitization. This technique not only enables surficial graphitized LCF preparation at a relatively low temperature of 1200 °C but also avoids additional treatments used in conventional carbon fiber production. The LCFs were then used as electrode materials in a supercapacitor assembly. Electrochemical measurements confirmed that LCF-0.4, a sample with a relatively low specific surface area of 89.9 m<sup>2</sup> g<sup>-1</sup>, exhibited the best electrochemical properties. The supercapacitor with LCF-0.4 had a specific capacitance of 10.7 F g<sup>-1</sup> at 0.5 A g<sup>-1</sup>, a power density of 869.5 W kg<sup>-1</sup>, an energy density of 15.7 Wh kg<sup>-1</sup>, and a capacitance retention of 100% after 1500 cycles, even without activation.
